To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the BP10 gene, which codes for an embryonic protein homologous to BMP-1 and tolloid, is expressed during the early cleavage stages in a spatially and temporally restricted way.

a gene coding for an enzyme with a catalytic domain typical of the human protein BMP1 and of the Drosophilatolloid gene product is expressed at the blastula and mesenchyme blastula transition stages of the sea urchins Strongylocentrotus purpuratus, Lytechinus pictus, and Paracentrotus lividus.
a cDNA encoding a secreted metalloprotease was isolated from sea urchin embryos and that the protein is synthesized in the presumptive ectomesoderm.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of a new protease, BP10, that is synthesized and secreted in a limited area and at a precise stage during sea urchins embryogenesis, and which may be involved in ectoderm patterning.
the study of the role played by a gene in the differentiation of the sea urchins embryo.
the characterization of a novel protease which is expressed in the ectodermal territory during the early stages of sea urchin development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BP10 gene product is a protease with a role in ectoderm differentiation and subsequent patterning.
the BP10 protein might play a role in the formation of the dorsal-ventral axis in the sea  urchin embryo, and that the tolloid gene might be the sea urchins homologue of the BP10.
the sea urchins and the flies are not so far apart after all.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have found an early embryonic protein with a structure similar to that of a human protease involved in the regulation of bone formation, a Drosophila gene product required for correct dorso-ventral pattering, and an embryonic protein that might be involved in the differentiation of the ectoderm in sea urchins.
the sea urchins and Drosophila have a conserved mechanism of gene regulation in the early development of their embryos.
we isolated the sea urchins' BMP-1 gene, and showed that it is expressed in the ectodermal domain of the embryo, and it has a role in the development of this tissue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have isolated a gene that is expressed in a spatially limited domain in the blastula stage sea urchin.
the sea urchins, like other deuterostomes, have BMP-1/Tolloid-like proteins.
the sea urchins are a great model for studying embryonic development.
